title: Decide whether http_request should be an INFO span, not DEBUG, now that two INFO spans exist
design:
Split off from bead mimid-1wgh.46.20.1.1, which said this was worth deciding
separately. That bead is closed: the provider_auth span it asked for is in,
at INFO.

THE QUESTION. http.rs:144 opens `http_request` with
tracing::debug_span!, so a collector sees it only with RUST_LOG=debug. It
carries method, route, status and elapsed_ms -- the per-request latency and
status an operator reading traces expects.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE IT WAS FILED. Two spans are now at INFO and cover the
interop-interesting cases: `protocol_request` for every /v1/ request that
reaches a handler, and `provider_auth` for every one carrying a `From`
header, refusals included. So [telemetry] with no RUST_LOG does now yield
traces, which was the operator complaint behind the original bead. What is
still missing at the default level is status and latency per request, and
any span at all for the paths that are neither /v1/ nor refused (the
directory, JMAP, proxyDownload).

MY RECOMMENDATION: LEAVE IT AT DEBUG, and this bead is the record of why
rather than a request to change it.

  - http_request wraps EVERY request, including the JMAP traffic an
    agent's polling generates, so INFO would multiply the span volume a
    collector takes by whatever the client load is. The /v1/ spans are
    bounded by peer traffic; this one is not.
  - The two facts it adds, status and elapsed_ms, also exist as metrics
    (http_requests by route and status, http_duration by route;
    `record_metrics`), exported continuously and unaffected by RUST_LOG.
    An operator who wants rates and latencies has them there.
  - docs/operating.md now states which spans are at which level and says
    RUST_LOG=info,mimid_server=debug turns this one on, so the
    expectation gap that produced the original bead is closed by
    documentation rather than by a default change.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: a real deployment that wants per-request traces
and cannot run at debug because the TEXT log at debug is too loud. That is
a real shape -- the two goals came apart once spans could go to a collector
instead of to stdout -- and the fix would then be a separate switch
([telemetry] span_level, say, or a filter for the OTel layer distinct from
the fmt layer's) rather than moving the span's level. Filing that would be
the follow-on, not this.

Also open, and smaller: a refused request has `provider_auth` but no
`http_request`, so its trace has no status or route. The alternative the
original bead listed -- moving provider_auth::check INSIDE the trace layer
-- would fix the shape properly and nest provider_auth under http_request.
It was not done because router() in http.rs applies the trace layer itself
and every test that calls router() would have to pass the check middleware
through it. Worth doing if the layer order is being touched for another
reason.
